name: F01 FENCE_OPEN: no guard after the backtick run
why: the near-miss clock row (a refused 50,000-backtick line takes seconds) and the document rows

name: F02 FENCE_OPEN: no guard after the tilde run
why: the near-miss clock row on tildes and the tilde document rows

name: F03 FENCE_OPEN: the backtick guard looks for a tilde
why: a backtick run followed by a tilde is refused (the enumeration) and a long refused line is quadratic again (the clock)

name: F04 FENCE_OPEN: the tilde guard looks for a backtick
why: a tilde run followed by a backtick is refused and a long refused tilde line is quadratic

name: F05 FENCE_OPEN: the backtick guard is positive
why: only a run followed by another backtick can match: the enumeration

name: F06 FENCE_OPEN: both guards refuse either fence character
why: ```~~~ stops being a fence: the enumeration

name: F07 FENCE_OPEN: the guards refuse a word character
why: an info string that starts at the run (```r) stops being a fence: the enumeration

name: F08 FENCE_OPEN: the backtick guard reads a backtick AND a CR (same answers, still quadratic)
why: the language is unchanged, so only a clock row can notice: the guard passes at every split but the last, and (.*) re-reads the tail

name: F09 FENCE_OPEN: the backtick guard reads two backticks (same answers, linear)
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: a longest run is never followed by a backtick, so the guard passes where it did; one split short of it is the only extra attempt, one pass of (.*), so the cost stays linear

name: F10 FENCE_OPEN: a run of 3 to 40
why: a run of 64 or 100 is refused: the gap grid

name: F11 FENCE_OPEN: a run of two is enough
why: ``` needs three: the enumeration

name: F12 FENCE_OPEN: the rest may hold U+2028
why: a fence line with a line separator is a fence: the enumeration

name: F13 FENCE_OPEN: the rest is not anchored
why: a CR after the run no longer refuses the line: the enumeration

name: F14 FENCE_OPEN: the indent is at most three spaces
why: a four-space or tab indent stops being read (the comment says it is NOT ` {0,3}`): the enumeration

name: F15 FENCE_OPEN: the indent is spaces only
why: a tab-indented fence stops being one: the enumeration

name: I01 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: no guard after the run

name: I02 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the guard looks for a tilde
why: a backtick run followed by a tilde is refused and a long refused line is quadratic

name: I03 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the guard is positive
why: only a run followed by another backtick can match: the enumeration

name: I04 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the guard reads a backtick AND a CR (same answers, still quadratic)
why: language unchanged: only the clock row notices

name: I05 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: a run of 3 to 40
why: a run of 64 or 100 is refused: the gap grid

name: I06 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the indent is blanks and tabs only
why: a form feed, a no-break space or a line terminator before the run stops being indent: the wide enumeration

name: I07 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the rest is not anchored
why: a CR after the run no longer refuses the line: the enumeration

name: I08 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: the guard reads two backticks (same answers, linear)
why: ARGUED EQUIVALENT: as F09

name: I09 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: a run of two is enough
why: ``` needs three: the enumeration

name: I10 INDENTED_CELL_FENCE_OPEN: an indent is required
why: a column-0 fence stops being read: the enumeration

name: D01 DIV_FENCE: no guard after the colon run

name: D02 DIV_FENCE: the guard looks for a backtick
why: a long refused colon line is quadratic again

name: D03 DIV_FENCE: the guard is positive

why: a run of 64 or 100 is refused: the gap grid

why: a bare ::: closer stops being a fence: the enumeration

name: D08 DIV_FENCE: the rest is not anchored

name: D09 DIV_FENCE: a run of two is enough
